acme-poc: hey team, hitting embedding failures & big latency spikes since yesterday evening. Our app targets eu-west but traces show some requests served from us-east. some responses return embedding length 768 but our model expects 1536 so downstream inference breaks.

ashley (Support): sorry about that — can you paste a failing request/response (redact keys)? also which model/endpoint and approx qps?

acme-poc: here's a sanitized curl we used:```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.host/eu-west/v1/embeddings" \-H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \-d '{"model":"text-embedding-3-large","input":["test sentence"]}'
```response headers include:```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: application/json
x-redwood-served-region: us-east-1
```and body:```json
{"data":[{"embedding":[...768 floats...] }],"model":"text-embedding-3-large"}
```we expected 1536 floats. qps ~150 during spike, usually 20.

ashley (Support): thanks. can you confirm if you set any region header or custom routing? also does this happen for single-item calls or only when batching?

acme-poc: we don't set explicit region headers, we rely on the eu-west base URL. single-item calls sometimes succeed, but bulk batch jobs show the dimension mismatch ~30% of the time during peak.

ashley (Support): stepping in to escalate to ML infra/serving. @kevin can you take a look? sounds like possible routing fallback/replica mismatch.

kevin (ML Eng): on it. initial hypothesis: capacity spillover in eu-west causing some requests to be routed to a different model variant in us-east with a different embedding dimension (e.g., quantized small variant). requesting logs for thread id later.

deploy-bot: routing-event: request_id=rvk-7790 region_hint=eu-west routed_region=us-east fallback_reason=capacity_exhausted

kevin (ML Eng): can you share the exact request_id from a failing response header (x-redwood-request-id) and approximate timestamps? that helps pull routing decisions. also, do you see model name exact in response body? sometimes we serve a lighter variant name in body.

acme-poc: one example request id `rvk-7790` timestamp `1954301154`. model in body was `text-embedding-3-large` (but dims 768).

janet (SRE): digging into routing logs for that interval. initial trace shows eu-west pool hit full concurrency at 19:12 UTC, autoscaler did not add capacity fast enough -> smart-router applied fallback_policy=region_fallback which picks compatible variant if exact match unavailable. there was a bug where variant mapping table for embeddings returned a compact-quantized alias that uses 768 dims — causing mismatch.

kevin (ML Eng): confirmed. mapping table had an outdated entry for `text-embedding-3-large`->`text-embedding-3-large-quant-small` in fallback list. that variant returns 768 vectors. this is why single calls sometimes worked (they hit eu-west), but batched jobs hit fallback when eu-west saturated.

ashley (Support): immediate mitigation options: 1) advise customer to pin to dedicated variant in eu-west (e.g., `text-embedding-3-large@eu-west` or use Dedicated capacity) 2) short-term: set header `X-Redwood-Preferred-Region: eu-west` to prefer local region routing 3) patch on our side to avoid returning mismatched variants for embeddings (blocking change). which do you prefer?

acme-poc: we'd prefer quick fix without rearchitecting. header option ok temporarily, but need permanent fix. also worried about silent dimension changes breaking production. can you provide repro steps so we can validate after fix?

kevin (ML Eng): plan: (a) roll a hotfix to variant mapping to remove 768-dim fallback for this model — deployment in 30m with canary; (b) add a heuristic to block fallback variants whose embedding dimension != primary model; (c) ops to bump eu-west min capacity to reduce spillover.

janet (SRE): I'll coordinate autoscaling tuning and add rate alerts when region_util > 85% to avoid future cold spillovers.

ashley (Support): repro steps for you to validate: 1) run a controlled burst to eu-west target endpoint with batch size 64 and qps=120 for 60s (we'll reproduce saturation). example script:```bash
for i in {1..120}; do \n  python -c "import requests, json; print(requests.post('https://api.redwood.host/eu-west/v1/embeddings', headers={'Authorization':'Bearer REDACTED','Content-Type':'application/json'}, json={'model':'text-embedding-3-large','input':['a']*64}).headers)" &\ndone
wait
```2) watch for responses with `x-redwood-served-region` != `eu-west` and check body embedding length.

acme-poc: will run after you deploy. can you confirm when hotfix goes out?

kevin (ML Eng): hotfix deployed to canary at 1954301225. canary traffic ~5% routed. initial logs show mapping table updated and heuristic active. no more route to 768 variants in canary. full rollout scheduled at 1954301260 after 2m canary monitoring.

deploy-bot: rollout-event: mapping-fix v2026.03.15-hotfix canary=5% start_ts=1954301225

janet (SRE): monitoring: eu-west util dropped after throttles and additional capacity added. alerts suppressed for canary window.

kevin (ML Eng): full rollout complete at 1954301260. verified zero requests routed to 768-dim variants for `text-embedding-3-large`.

acme-poc: reran our batch test — all responses served from eu-west and dims 1536. latency back to normal. thanks.

ashley (Support): closing loop, root cause: capacity exhaustion in eu-west + outdated fallback mapping allowed incompatible compact variant. fix: mapping table hotfix + heuristic to validate embedding dims before fallback. follow-ups: add a pre-deploy test to validate variant compatibility and increase min capacity in eu-west pools.

kevin (ML Eng): opened infra ticket INF-4829 for permanent fix and load-testing plan. janet will add autoscale tuning notes to runbook.

ashley (Support): I'll send summary to you and your CSM and mark this resolved. feel free to reopen if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
